A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PP/RMD/APP research work. Their text, equations, figures, table, and Appendices A–F support a reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v3 reports original Beach Bar Process experiments comparing APP with fixed-base RMD, including exploitability and policy trajectories in Figure 2.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experimental results in Figure 2, with experimental settings documented in Appendix F.

M1.justification: The PP update, regularized objective, RMD update, and APP procedure remain unchanged. Pseudocode is reorganized; asynchronous feedback is discussed only as a possible future extension.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Beach Bar Process on a discrete one-dimensional torus. The new symmetric-transition example in v4 is a mathematical counterexample, not an additional evaluated task.

E2.justification: Fixed-base RMD remains the empirical comparator against APP in Figure 2. Additions and corrections to Table 1 concern literature comparisons, not methods newly evaluated by this work.

E3.justification: The horizon, state/action spaces, learning rate, regularization and transition parameters, uniform initialization, exploitability metric, and plotted update intervals are retained. The algorithms/settings paragraph moves from Section 5 to Appendix F.

E4.justification: The existing fixed-base and inner-iteration comparisons are retained. No additional documented ablation, robustness experiment, or sensitivity study accompanies the brief instability remark added to Appendix F.

E5.justification: Both Appendix F sections explicitly report one run per experimental setting because APP is deterministic. Neither version adds repeated-run statistics, confidence intervals, or significance testing.

E6.justification: Figures 1 and 2 retain the same plotted results. New Remark F.1 reports a qualitative finding: small inner-loop length τ can cause outer-loop instability when 1−λη is close to one. No additional measurements accompany this statement.

T1.justification: v4 reformulates monotonicity from arbitrary mean-field/policy pairs in v3 Assumption 2.2 to policy-induced occupancies in Assumption 2.4. It adds a strictness definition, a two-state symmetric-transition counterexample, and an exploitability–KL bound in Section 4.2. The principal convergence theorems and Appendix B–E proof arguments otherwise remain essentially intact.

C1.justification: The headline contributions remain PP last-iterate convergence under non-strict monotonicity, exponential RMD convergence to regularized equilibrium, and APP with empirical convergence. The rewritten abstract makes these distinctions more explicit without introducing a different principal contribution.

C2.justification: New Section 6 explicitly leaves APP last-iterate convergence unproved and discusses absent statistical, computational-cost, scalability, and function-approximation guarantees. Remark 2.2 clarifies the exclusion of mean-field-dependent transitions. Section 4.2 qualifies finite-iteration advantages because the permitted step size can be small; asynchronous feedback and instability conditions receive new discussion.

D1.justification: Both versions disclose the same hardware, Python implementation, implementation attribution to Fabian et al., numerical settings, and initialization. Relocating the algorithms/settings paragraph to Appendix F adds no new reproducibility information or resource access.

R1.justification: v4 adds Ao et al. (2023), Geist et al. (2022), and J. Huang et al. (2024). Table 1 adds the concavity-based Geist entry and changes the Angiuli entries' LIC classification from affirmative to negative. Comparisons with local optimization guarantees and finite-iteration rates are refined; the central research positioning remains.

P1.justification: The abstract and selected passages are rewritten, the problem setup is reordered, experimental details move to Appendix F, and limitations and funding sections are added. Author information and reference wording change, while most narrative and appendix prose is retained.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from two columns to a single column, with extensive equation and theorem-box reflow. APP and RMD pseudocode are separated, while the standalone PP pseudocode is removed but its defining equation retained. Table 1 moves to Appendix A and loses its iteration-count column. Figures are resized and relocated without changing their plotted content.

improvement.justification: v4 improves scope clarification through its limitations section, step-size caveat, and symmetric-transition example. However, the new Section 4.2 bound appears to make unregularized exploitability vanish at a regularized equilibrium, conflicting with Section 4.5 and the retained RMD plateau in Figure 2b. The PDF supplies no qualification resolving this inconsistency. These explanatory gains and the new theoretical concern prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
